entries.effect: the border of an annotation, over the dictionary that carries it: the /Border array of PDF 1.7 Table 164 for the line width, and the /BS dictionary of Table 8.44 for the style and the dash pattern.  Reached through -[PDFAnnotation border], which is the only path - PDFBorder.h declares no initializer at all - and nil there is a measured answer: a border is answered for an annotation whose dictionary names a /Border or a /BS whatever its subtype, otherwise for the geometry subtypes /Circle /FreeText /Ink /Line /Square, otherwise for a /Widget whose /MK names a border colour the format's four component counts allow, and nil otherwise.  The two setters the header declares are NOT implemented, and no method is missing because of it: this port reads documents and a setter here would answer without changing the file behind it, which is the same boundary PDFAnnotation's -bounds has

entries.effect: the /BS /S name read through a table and not as an ordinal: /S is solid, /D dashed, /B beveled, /I inset, /U underline, and a name the format does not list answers solid.  All five names and the unlisted one are measured (bs-s, bs-d, bs-b, bs-i, bs-u, bs-q), because the enum's order and the format's names run the same way and reading one as the position would fit the same data.  The setter is not implemented; see the class row

entries.effect: the /BS /W when the dictionary has one, and the THIRD number of the /Border array when it does not - measured on bs-width-only, which writes /Border [0 0 7] beside /W 5 and answers 5.  The third element and not the last: /Border [1 2 3 4] answers 3.  The two corner radii are not read: /Border [5 7 2] answers 2.  A negative width is a width: [0 0 -2.5] answers -2.5.  A zero is a value: [0 0 0] answers 0.  The default is 1, and three fixtures fix it where the third element is missing.  A /W that is not a number is refused and the width falls through, while the style beside it still answers - measured on bs-width-string.  The setter is not implemented; see the class row

entries.effect: the /BS /D array of numbers, and nil for every style but dashed - bs-dash-solid carries /S /S beside /D [4 1] and answers nil.
